purpose: Dicyclomine is used to treat irritable bowel syndrome (IBS). It helps relieve stomach cramps, pain, and spasms in your gut. It can make your belly feel much more comfortable by calming down an overactive or cramping intestine.
how_it_works: Your intestines are controlled by tiny nerve signals that can sometimes go into overdrive, causing painful cramps and spasms. Dicyclomine blocks those nerve signals so your gut muscles can relax. Think of it like a 'off switch' for the overactive cramping in your belly.
common_side_effects: Dry mouth, blurry vision, dizziness, drowsiness, constipation, difficulty urinating, upset stomach, and feeling flushed or warm. These are very common and usually mild. Drinking water and sucking on sugar-free candy can help with dry mouth.
warnings: Do not use this medication if you have glaucoma, trouble urinating, severe constipation, myasthenia gravis, or a blockage in your stomach or intestines. It can make you very drowsy, so be careful driving or using machinery. Avoid alcohol while taking this medicine. Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, breastfeeding, or elderly, as extra caution is needed. Do NOT give to babies under 6 months old — it can be very dangerous for infants.
typical_dosing: Adults usually start with 20 mg taken by mouth 4 times a day. Your doctor may increase your dose to 40 mg four times a day if needed and if you are tolerating it well. Always follow exactly what your doctor tells you, and take it with or without food.
